title: Source collections
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/source-collections, application/json: one part of the complete listing of the collections the adapter can reach through one connection, sent when the connection is made, whenever that set changes, and whenever a listed collection's environment_ref changes, comes or goes. The control plane records each collection's latest environment_ref from the latest listing that names the collection; a listing that leaves it out says the collection has no environment definition. An adapter that cannot read a collection's environment definition leaves that collection out of every part of the listing and sends the listing's last part with complete: false, so the listing disconnects nothing, since only a complete listing does, and the collection keeps its record and its environment_ref until a later listing names it. Every part of a listing names the same connection_id. A collection is a place at the source that items are listed from, such as a project, a board or a project on a code host. Collections belong to the connection that listed them, keyed on the adapter, the connection and the collection's ref. A connection is made when the control plane accepts a linked connect return, as connection_id in definitions.schema.json says; the first listing after that reports its collections, and may be one empty part with complete: true. A collection is not active by being listed: it is linked when a person assigns it to a workspace in the control plane, and the adapter learns that from the change feed (changes.schema.json). A complete listing, every part from 1 to n arrived and part n saying complete: true, disconnects, as sources/disconnect would, every collection of that connection it left out whose last change is older than its started_at, and closes no other connection's collection. A ref is unique among the integration's live collections. A listing that names a ref live under another connection of the integration ends that collection, as a disconnect would, and creates a new one under this connection; nothing moves between connections. A grant is linked to at most one live connection, so this happens only when the source has really moved the collection between grants (connect-pass.schema.json). Ending the other connection's collection ends that one collection only, never its connection. When the ended collection was linked to a workspace, the change feed carries an unlinked entry for its ref, followed by the new collection's entries once it is linked. The ref names one live collection at a time, so the last entry per ref stays its current state. An adapter lists only refs the source grants that connection when it reads them. A stale listing that names a ref again would end the other connection's collection in the same way. Items, sources/disconnect and the change feed name a collection by its ref alone, and comments name an item by its item_ref; definitions.schema.json says which collection answers each. The control plane refuses a connection_id that it does not hold for this adapter, 403 connection_unknown, with the same signed body for every cause, and a pending connection is answered 403 connection_unknown on every request but POST /v1/connections/disconnect, which ends it with the signed 204 (refusal.schema.json); then a connection that ended, 409 connection_ended, final for that connection; then a connection whose organisation is out of use for now, 409 connection_suspended, which is not final: the adapter changes no state and sends the listing again on its periodic check. On success the control plane answers a signed 204 with no body. It is signed with the adapter's access key as definitions.schema.json describes. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401; definitions.schema.json has the replay rule. A member this schema does not define is refused, invalid_request.

version.description: The document format. The control plane refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the adapter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.

connection_id.description: The connection the collections are reached through, as its connect pass named it (connect-pass.schema.json).

collections.description: This part's collections, at most 100. A listing of none, complete, says the adapter reaches no collection through that connection.

url.description: The collection's page at the source.

title.description: The collection's name at the source.

target.description: Where a change for the collection's items would go. Absent when the adapter names none.

environment_ref.description: The id of the collection's environment definition, as definitions.schema.json describes it. Absent when the collection has none.

listing.description: Which part of which listing this is.
